time.desc: The second instance of a civil dispute involving sexual harassment charges in a university library was pronounced. The court rejected the appeal and upheld the original verdict, confirming that the civil claims related to the charges were not supported.

The university involved issued a review and disposition notice: revoking the disciplinary sanctions against the accused party, and at the same time concluded that "there are many irregularities in the thesis of the accused party but do not constitute academic misconduct and degree maintenance", and simultaneously announced the accountability of relevant responsible personnel.
The parties involved expressed their defense through social platforms and had public verbal conflicts with netizens/related parties, which heated up public opinion again.

The party involved posted on social platforms and quickly denied the statement that he had "passed a certain type of public office/qualification examination", triggering a new round of controversy surrounding his integrity and qualification review.
At the same time as the judicial proceedings of the university involved were concluded, the party committee secretary was replaced, and the new secretary took office.
The university involved focused on refuting many key online rumors in the report
The university involved formed a five-member expert team to complete the review and announced the scale of the investigation and the conclusion that the paper did not involve plagiarism.
The accuser spoke out intensively on social platforms to communicate with the outside world and defended himself. The incident was filed in the relevant false accusation theme archives by We Media.

The judicial process of the university involved ended, the demerit penalty imposed on the accused was revoked, many relevant personnel were held accountable, and the accuser’s master’s degree was still found to be qualified.
In the review notification, the school suspended the relevant tutors' enrollment qualifications for two years, and gave several managers intra-party warnings or admonishments.
The school clarified in the briefing that the rumor that a relative of the accuser holds a certain title within the school is untrue.

The school issued another notice, confirming that the accuser's paper contained more than 100 irregularities but no academic misconduct was found, and it complied with the degree awarding regulations.

The school established a five-member expert team to complete the reexamination, investigated 21 people, reviewed 91 pieces of evidence, and determined that the paper was not plagiarized and the degree was not revoked.
